quick: PD: IR 0.125 mg TID titrated to 1.5-4.5 mg/day; ER 0.375 mg once daily
With or without food (food may reduce nausea)
Use only if clearly needed (limited human data)
Reduce dose / extend interval in renal impairment (renally cleared)
summary: Pramipexole is a non-ergot dopamine agonist (preferential D3 receptor affinity) used for Parkinson's disease and moderate-to-severe restless legs syndrome. It is available in immediate-release (multiple daily doses) and extended-release (once daily) forms. It is largely renally eliminated, so doses are adjusted for renal impairment. Key risks are sudden sleep onset, impulse-control disorders, orthostatic hypotension and hallucinations.
indications: Treatment of Parkinson's disease (early and advanced; ER and IR)
Treatment of moderate-to-severe primary Restless Legs Syndrome (IR)

dosage.d: Start 0.125 mg three times daily; titrate every 5-7 days to 0.5-1.5 mg TID (1.5-4.5 mg/day)
Start 0.375 mg once daily; titrate every 5-7 days up to max 4.5 mg/day
0.125 mg once daily 2-3 h before bedtime; may increase every 4-7 days to max 0.5 mg/day
dosage.n: Lowest effective dose; watch for augmentation

dosage.d: Reduce starting dose and frequency by CrCl; lower max dose
dosage.n: ER not recommended if CrCl <30; severe impairment: adjust IR carefully

admin: Titrate slowly to minimize nausea and orthostatic hypotension
Take with food if nausea occurs
Swallow ER tablets whole; do not chew, crush or divide
Discontinue gradually (taper) to avoid withdrawal/dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome
moa: Pramipexole is a non-ergot dopamine agonist with high relative specificity and full intrinsic activity at the D2 subfamily of dopamine receptors, binding with higher affinity to D3 than D2 or D4 subtypes. In Parkinson's disease it is believed to act by stimulating striatal dopamine receptors, compensating for nigrostriatal dopamine deficiency.

relative: Cardiovascular disease / predisposition to orthostatic hypotension
History of impulse-control disorder or compulsive behaviors
monitor: Excessive daytime sleepiness / sudden sleep onset
Impulse-control behaviors (gambling, hypersexuality, shopping, binge eating)

preg: Limited human data; use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Dopamine agonists may also interfere with lactation.
lact: Not recommended; pramipexole inhibits prolactin secretion and is likely to suppress lactation, and excretion into milk is expected.
renal: Largely eliminated unchanged by the kidneys. Reduce starting dose, dosing frequency and maximum dose according to creatinine clearance; the extended-release form is not recommended in patients with CrCl <30 mL/min.
hepatic: No dose adjustment needed; hepatic metabolism is minimal.

major: Dopamine antagonists (antipsychotics, metoclopramide) - reduce pramipexole efficacy; avoid
moderate: Cimetidine and other organic cation transport inhibitors (e.g., ranolazine) - increase pramipexole levels; may need dose reduction
Sedatives, alcohol, other CNS depressants - additive somnolence
minor: Levodopa - may need levodopa dose reduction when adding pramipexole
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food can reduce nausea and delays peak.

serious: Impulse-control disorders (pathological gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive shopping/eating)
rare: Dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome on discontinuation
emergency: Sudden sleep onset while driving/operating machinery

monitoring: Blood pressure (lying and standing) during titration
Assess for daytime sleepiness and sudden sleep onset
Ask regularly about impulse-control and compulsive behaviors
Watch for hallucinations and, in RLS, for augmentation
counsel: Do not drive or operate machinery until you know how it affects you - it can cause sudden sleep
Tell your doctor about new urges to gamble, shop, eat or sexual urges (impulse-control disorders)
Do not stop suddenly - the dose must be tapered
Avoid alcohol; take with food if it upsets your stomach
pk: Symptomatic benefit over days to weeks of titration
IR dosed three times daily; ER once daily
Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect ER from moisture/light
pearls: Non-ergot D2/D3 agonist - no ergot-related fibrotic/valvular risk
Impulse-control disorders and sudden sleep onset are class-defining safety issues - counsel and ask about them
Renally cleared - dose by creatinine clearance; ER not recommended if CrCl <30
Used for both Parkinson's disease and restless legs syndrome; watch for RLS augmentation
Taper to stop - abrupt withdrawal can cause dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome (DAWS)
missed: For ER once-daily: if missed, skip it and take the next dose at the usual time (do not take two). For IR: take when remembered unless close to the next dose, then skip. Do not double up.
overdose: There is limited overdose experience; expected effects include nausea, vomiting, hyperkinesia, agitation, hallucinations and hypotension. No specific antidote; provide supportive care, cardiovascular monitoring, and consider a dopamine antagonist (e.g., a phenothiazine) for severe stimulation. Activated charcoal may help if recent ingestion.
